findings.problem: status is a bare String, allowing any value including invalid transitions. The LeaseWorkflow typestate permits states like {status:"sent",is_sent:false} or {status:"draft",is_sent:true}.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid lease lifecycle states are constructible and silently persist; callers cannot rely on status meaning anything without manual invariant checks.
findings.fix: Replace String status with a sealed LeaseStatus enum (Draft, Validated, Sent, Revoked) and remove is_sent/is_validated booleans. Only the enum variant encodes the lifecycle.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent flags that do not form a proper typestate. All four boolean combinations are valid, but the domain has fewer legitimate states.
findings.failure_mode: A lease can be both validated and unsent, or neither validated nor sent but marked sent_at_epoch_ms, violating domain invariants without compiler enforcement.
findings.fix: Collapse is_validated and is_sent into a single LeaseStatus enum. Remove both bool fields. This makes every representable state a valid state.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from the lifecycle state. It can be Some when status != "sent".
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can hold a timestamp for a non-sent lease, producing incorrect audit trails and violating the invariant that a sent timestamp only exists when sent.
findings.fix: Move the epoch timestamp into the Sent variant of a LeaseStatus enum so it only exists when the lease is actually sent. Example: enum LeaseStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: id is a bare String with no domain newtype. There are no invariants on id format, uniqueness, or lifetime.
findings.failure_mode: Id values from different domains or invalid formats mix freely; no compile-time distinction between lease ids, workflow ids, or other string identifiers.
findings.fix: Introduce a LeaseId newtype: pub struct LeaseId(String); or use an existing Uuid/OpaqueId type. All APIs should accept/return LeaseId instead of String.

findings.problem: status is a String instead of an enum, meaning mark_sent can only mutate by writing a magic string literal.
findings.failure_mode: Typos in string literals (e.g., "snt" instead of "sent") silently produce invalid states. Refactoring the status vocabulary requires hunting for string literals across the codebase.
findings.fix: Replace with a LeaseStatus enum. mark_sent becomes a constructor returning LeaseWorkflow { id, status: LeaseStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: now() } }

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate lifecycle state without domain methods.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can directly assign item.status = "foo" or item.is_sent = false, bypassing any workflow logic and creating invalid states.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Provide domain constructors and state-transition methods (e.g., fn validate(), fn send()) as the only way to mutate the struct.

residual_risk: The entire domain model uses primitive types (String, bool) instead of type-enforced invariants. Every state transition is a string assignment with zero compile-time safety. This is the canonical 'invalid state lease typestate' anti-pattern. The code is functionally correct for a trivial single-call scenario but architecturally broken for any real system where invariants must be enforced by the type system.
